items.title: Run the CLI through a symlinked path (npm .bin link, node_modules/<pkg> under pnpm)
body: npm installs `bin` as a symlink `node_modules/.bin/houserules -> ../houserules/bin/houserules.mjs`. Node resolves `import.meta.url` through the symlink but keeps `process.argv[1]` as the `.bin` path, so the entry guard in `bin/houserules.mjs` never matches and the CLI exits 0 without output.

Fix: compare against `realpathSync(process.argv[1])` in the guard; apply the same idiom in `template/tools/kb.mjs` and `template/tools/backlog.mjs`. Regression test: run the bin through a symlink and expect the manifest.
Verified live on 2026-08-31 with `npm exec --package=git+file://<clone> -- houserules files`: 0 lines, exit 0; the direct path prints the manifest.

Probe of 2026-09-01 under pnpm 11.18.0 (`pnpm add --save-exact git+file://<clone>` in a scratch project): `pnpm exec houserules files` and `pnpm dlx git+file://<clone> files` print the manifest, because pnpm's bin shim execs the real path under `node_modules/.pnpm/`; `node node_modules/houserules/bin/houserules.mjs files` through the package symlink prints nothing and exits 0. The defect is independent of the package manager.

items.title: Report invalid JSON in knowledge and backlog files as a usage error
body: `loadBase` and `loadBacklog` let `JSON.parse` errors escape as stack traces (`SyntaxError: Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1`); `tools/kb.sh render` inside `init` then dies with the raw trace.

Fix: `readJson` raises a `UsageError` that names the file and the parse message, as `audit --report` already does for a malformed report. `init` keeps failing with a non-zero exit; the init test `lets a render failure on broken project data propagate as a real error` stays valid.

items.title: Port process.evals-rerun with its co-change check and evals record from tag-pilot
body: tag-pilot `fc3241b` (2026-08-31) adds the rule `process.evals-rerun`: re-run every `.claude/evals/` scenario whenever the implementer or task-reviewer template or a scenario changes; a `co-change` check fails the audit until `.claude/evals/record.json` changes with them; the record keys runs by the templates' git blob ids. The orchestrating skill gains a 'Template evaluation' procedure and the branch reviewer compares the record's blob ids with HEAD.

Blocked until PR #42 is merged (owner instruction). Then port it to `template/` (knowledge entry, orchestrating skill bullet, branch-reviewer check, and the `kb.mjs` co-change lines if the drift holds them) and diff the remaining drift.

items.title: Switch this repository to pnpm and set the workspace up like tag-pilot
body: Owner ruling of 2026-09-01 (docs/design.md §5.7): use pnpm only, never npm or npx.

Scope: exact `node` and `pnpm` pins in `mise.toml` written by `mise use`; `pnpm-lock.yaml` replaces `package-lock.json`; `pnpm-workspace.yaml` for the pnpm settings; the mise tasks `setup`, `test`, `lint`, and `audit` as in tag-pilot; README, knowledge entries, and the development commands name pnpm. `template/` stays dependency-free.
The batch 2 spec fixes the file list and settles the commitlint commit-msg hook.

items.title: Capture the render child's stderr in init instead of inheriting it
body: `install` in `bin/houserules.mjs` spawns `tools/kb.mjs render` with an inherited stderr, so the init test on broken project data prints one usage-error line into the suite output (tests/init.test.mjs, 'lets a render failure on broken project data propagate as a real error').
Fix: spawn with `stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']` and put the child's stderr into the thrown error; the test asserts the message and the suite output stays silent.
Source: task 3 re-review and the batch 2 branch review (2026-09-01).

items.title: Enforce the commit body line limit in the commits check
body: The `commits` check of `tools/kb.sh audit` tests the subject pattern and `body_absent` only; two controller commits with 190- and 227-character body lines passed the batch 2 audits as '9 commits checked'. Only the commit-msg hook catches it, for commits made after it was installed.

Fix: add the optional key `body_line_max` (integer, minimum 1) to `$defs.check` in `knowledge/schema.json` and `template/knowledge/schema.json`; in the `commits` runner of `template/tools/kb.mjs`, fail a commit with a body line longer than the limit; regression tests for 100 and 101 characters and a `checkShape` case; `update --dir .`.

Ruled 2026-09-01 (docs/design.md §5.8): the same task sets `body_line_max: 100` on `process.conventional-commits` in `knowledge/process.json` and `template/knowledge/process.json`. Source: batch 2 branch review, violated_rules.

items.title: Agent template and deliverables refinements from the batch 2 retrospective
body: Deliverables schema (`template/.claude/schemas/deliverables.json` and the root copy): add an optional integer `exit` to `$defs.run`; the implementer template's Report section names it for every run whose exit code is evidence, and `output` stays verbatim (batch 2: exit codes were written into `output` as prose).

Implementer template `coverage`: 'one measure per target whenever the project has a coverage gate and the full suite ran, so the batch keeps a baseline; null only when the suite did not run' (batch 2 task 1 left it null and a fix round repaired it).

Orchestrating skill, dispatch protocol: a brief names no version number for a tool, action, or package (security-hygiene.exact-pins); it names the verification the implementer runs and shows placeholders such as `jdx/mise-action@<current major>` (batch 2 task 1 brief carried a stale `@v2`).
Source: batch 2 branch review, template_defects 2-4.

items.title: Audit report-field checks over a workspace of task reports
body: A branch has no single report, so the four report-field rows (deliverables-json, knowledge-first, dependency-vetting, verify-current-docs) come back `skipped` from `tools/kb.sh audit` and the branch reviewer judges them by hand from the task reports.

Fix: accept `--report` more than once, or add `--workspace <dir>` that reads every `task-*-report.json`; a report-field check passes when every report whose changed files trigger it sets the field, and names the offending report otherwise. Source: batch 2 branch review, template_defects 5.

items.title: Diff the audit range from the merge base
body: `changedFiles` in `template/tools/kb.mjs` diffs `base..head`, so the pull-request audit (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) sees unrelated files when main moves after the branch was cut. Inherited from tag-pilot's knowledge.yml.

Fix: `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR --merge-base <base> <head>` for the files, `git log <base>..<head>` for the commits; a test with a moved base. Source: batch 2 branch review, recommendations.

items.title: Report an unreadable .houserules.json as a usage error
body: `install` parses the stamp with raw `JSON.parse(readFileSync(markerPath))`; an unreadable `.houserules.json` escapes as a SyntaxError stack trace. `tests/init.test.mjs` (the test "propagates an unreadable marker, which is a defect and not a usage error") pins the current behavior until this item.

Fix: reuse `readJson` from `template/tools/lib/json-store.mjs` (it raises `UsageError` with `<path>: invalid JSON (...)`; the bin already imports from that module) and rewrite the pinning test the way HR-005 rewrote its predecessor.
Source: batch 3 task 1 review (2026-09-01); the branch review filed the missing item as its critical finding.

items.title: Carry the git stderr in the no-merge-base usage error
body: `gitDiff` in `template/tools/kb.mjs` reports every `git diff` failure as `no merge base between "<base>" and "<head>"` and discards the child stderr, so a different failure (a missing object in a shallow clone, repository corruption) is mislabeled and its diagnostic lost.
Fix: pipe the child stderr and include it in the `UsageError`, or use the no-merge-base text only when the stderr indicates it; sync the root copy; one test.
Deferred from batch 3 with the branch review’s reason: `rev` pre-validates both refs, so the remaining failure modes are exotic. Source: batch 3 branch review, minor 2 (2026-09-01).

items.title: Dispatch-protocol bullets: a brief carries the spec, a dispatch carries changed templates
body: Two additions to the orchestrating skill’s dispatch protocol (`template/.claude/skills/orchestrating/SKILL.md`, kit-owned, then `update --dir .`): a brief names every test and gate its spec task lists, verbatim or by pointer (batch 3 task 3’s brief dropped the seed-checkBase test and the gap cost a review round); when a batch edits an agent template, the dispatch message carries the changed instruction verbatim, because templates load at session start (batch 3’s branch review ran on the pre-branch template).
Consider seeding `process.brief-carries-the-spec` (added to the root knowledge at the batch 3 close) into `template/knowledge/process.json` in the same task.
Source: batch 3 branch review, template_defects 1 and 3 (2026-09-01).

items.title: A migration skill: move a pre-existing codebase’s knowledge into the houserules style
body: Owner request of 2026-09-01: when houserules is installed into a codebase that already has knowledge (CLAUDE.md prose, docs, wikis, comments, ad-hoc rules files), a skill in the payload explains how to migrate it: inventory the sources, split rule/invariant/gotcha/procedure/decision/history, write entries per the schema (summary is the rule, ≤160; body why/how/exceptions; source with date and by; verify paths; check where deterministic), extend areas, park the leftovers, delete the migrated originals, and gate with tools/kb.sh check plus render.

Shape to design in the batch spec: a kit-owned skill (template/.claude/skills/, overwritten by update) that the README’s install-to-existing section points to; likely with a worked example and the knowledge-base.* rules by pointer.
Candidate for batch 5 with its own spec gate.

items.title: Read settings.json through readJson in the bin
body: `mergeSettings` in `bin/houserules.mjs` still parses `.claude/settings.json` by hand and wraps the failure as `not readable JSON (...)`, a second wording for the failure class the stamp path now reports as `invalid JSON` through `readJson`.

Fix: `settings = readJson(path)` and drop the catch; the existing test asserts exit 2 and the file name only. Decide the one semantic change: an unreadable (not just invalid) settings.json then propagates as a plain Error, like the stamp.
Source: batch 4 task 1 review, minor (2026-09-01); deferred out of HR-010 because of that semantics decision.

items.title: Commit-msg hook rejects trailers; ship .githooks in the payload
body: The hook runs commitlint only, so a harness-injected Co-Authored-By trailer reached a batch 4 commit and was caught by hand (task 3); security-hygiene.no-coauthor is enforced only post-hoc by the audit.

Fix: a trailer gate in .githooks/commit-msg before commitlint (grep -qiE for Co-Authored-By → one error line, exit 1). Consider shipping .githooks in the kit payload (KIT_OWNED) so consumers get the gate; this repository has no template copy of the hook today.
Source: batch 4 branch review, template_defects 1 (2026-09-02).

items.title: A structured live_run field in task reports, with a recipe check
body: Live-run evidence has no structured field, so a missing scratch recipe is findable only in prose (batch 4 task 2). Add an optional live_run array (command, output, exit) to $defs.taskReport in both deliverables schema copies; give houserules.live-run-recipe a report-field check at warn on live_run; the implementer template names the field.
Source: batch 4 branch review, template_defects 2 (2026-09-02).

items.title: A mode field on tdd cycles: natural, mutation, or reconstructed
body: A tdd cycle cannot say how it was produced; batch 4 task 4 spent two report rounds wording the difference between a natural RED, a mutation proof, and a post-commit reconstruction. Add an optional mode enum (natural | mutation | reconstructed) to $defs.tddCycle in both schema copies and one implementer-template sentence: set mode when the cycle is not a natural pre-commit RED.
Source: batch 4 branch review, template_defects 3 (2026-09-02).

items.title: Co-change evidence names a record-only change plainly
body: When the then file itself matches the if glob, the co-change evidence is circular ("record.json changed with record.json"). In template/tools/kb.mjs: when the only if match is the then path, print "only <then> changed; the co-change is satisfied by definition"; otherwise exclude the then path from the listed if matches. Behavior unchanged; one test.
Source: batch 4 branch review, template_defects 4 (2026-09-02).

items.title: Area glob matching misses dot-segments under **
body: node:path matchesGlob excludes dot-segments under **: matchesGlob('template/.claude/skills/migrating-knowledge/SKILL.md', 'template/**') returns false (verified live in the batch 5 branch review). Every batch 5 audit ran without the template area: houserules.payload-runs-on-builtins dropped out of the audit package, and the rules loader never serves .claude/rules/template.md for template/.claude/** files.

Fix in template/tools/kb.mjs areaFiles (matchesGlob, ~line 106): wrap matchesGlob with a dot-inclusive variant, or a small globToRegExp with dot semantics. RED first: areasFor(['template/.claude/agents/implementer.md'], areas) must include 'template'. The fix ships in the payload; target repositories inherit it via update.
Source: batch 5 branch review, template_defects 1 (2026-09-02).

items.title: mergeSettings crashes on valid non-object JSON in settings.json
body: A .claude/settings.json containing null, a string, or a number passes readJson and then crashes with a plain TypeError stack at settings.hooks ??= {}. Pre-existing behavior, not regressed by batch 5 task 2.
Cover it with the CLI's one-line UsageError convention. RED first: a scratch settings.json containing null.
Source: batch 5 branch review, recommendation 2 (2026-09-02).

items.title: A verdict.text field for re-review prose; open lists only prior findings
body: verdict.open is a bare textList; batch 5 task-1-review-r1.json used it for a status sentence plus restatements of both new_breakage items, so state 'findings-remain' read as prior findings open when all eight were addressed and only new breakage remained.

Add an optional verdict.text for prose to $defs.reReview in .claude/schemas/deliverables.json (root and template). State in task-reviewer.md that open lists only prior findings still unaddressed and that new breakage lives only in new_breakage.
Changing task-reviewer.md triggers process.evals-rerun: re-run every scenario and append the run set to .claude/evals/record.json.
Source: batch 5 branch review, template_defects 2 (2026-09-02).

items.title: The stamp read crashes on a non-object .houserules.json
body: install reads the marker with 'existsSync(markerPath) ? readJson(markerPath) : { idPrefix: prefix }' and then touches marker.idPrefix; a .houserules.json holding null (or a string, a number, a boolean, an array) passes readJson and crashes with a raw stack at bin/houserules.mjs:185. Verified live at batch 6 task 3's HEAD commit ('fix(cli): reject a non-object settings.json as a usage error'): first init exit 0, 'printf null > .houserules.json', second init exit 1 with the stack.
Fix as HR-020's sibling: reject a non-object marker with the one-line UsageError convention ('<path>: not a JSON object'), RED first; the existing HR-010 stamp tests stay green.
Source: batch 6 task 3 review, minor 2 (2026-09-02).

items.title: Re-review dispatches carry the round-0 block; audits refuse a missing --ids
body: The batch 6 task 1 round-1 re-review dispatch omitted the Backlog: line and the --ids list, so task-1-audit-r1.json ran a narrowed package (27 rows; houserules.live-run-recipe and houserules.node-under-mise dropped). The reviewer caught it; round 2 was dispatched correctly, but nothing forces the block.

Fix: the orchestrating skill's re-review dispatch bullet requires the identical Knowledge:/Backlog:/--ids block as the round-0 dispatch; the task-reviewer template refuses to run an audit without --ids when the task's id list is non-empty.
Changing task-reviewer.md triggers process.evals-rerun: re-run every scenario and append the run set to .claude/evals/record.json.
Source: batch 6 branch review, template_defects 1 (2026-09-02).

items.title: Stamp an empty-range audit as vacuous
body: An audit with base == head (batch 6 task 1's report-only round 2) succeeds with vacuous deterministic rows ('0 commits checked', '0 files checked', 'not triggered') that read as positive evidence; the round-2 reviewer had to annotate them as vacuous by hand.
Fix in template/tools/kb.mjs: when the range holds no commits, set "empty_range": true in the audit summary and prefix the deterministic evidence strings with 'empty range:'. RED first.
Source: batch 6 branch review, template_defects 2 (2026-09-02).

items.title: Pin the two SEED_ONCE deliverables schema copies in sync
body: tests/dogfood.test.mjs pins every KIT_OWNED root copy byte-for-byte, but .claude/schemas/deliverables.json is SEED_ONCE: update never writes it, and its root and template copies are hand-synced. They differ only in the backlogId pattern (HR- vs WI-) by design.
Batch 7 hand-synced four new fields across both copies on manual diligence alone. Add a test that compares the copies modulo the known backlogId pattern difference, so a drift fails the suite.
Source: batch 7 task 3 review, controller note (2026-09-02).

items.title: The audit package admits area-matched entries that carry a check
body: The package builder (template/tools/kb.mjs:709) admits only standing entries and area-matched rule/invariant kinds, so the report-field check on houserules.live-run-recipe (kind procedure, area cli) never joins a range-derived package: the batch 7 branch audit carried no live_run row though the plan promised it. Task audits carried it only via --ids.

Fix: admit any area-matched entry that carries a check (e.g. e.check && areas.includes(e.area)), RED first with a regression test that a checked procedure joins the package; template first, root synced. Damage is minor today because the schema makes live_run required, which fails validate harder than the warn row.

Deferred out of batch 7 by the controller: audit-machinery semantics deserve full review rounds, not a post-branch-review patch. Source: batch 7 branch review, minor 1 + template_defects 1 (2026-09-02).

items.title: The stamp guard validates idPrefix as a string
body: readJsonObject accepts any plain object, so a .houserules.json holding an idPrefix that is a number passes the guard and the number flows into id generation. Owner-candidate: decide whether the stamp is fully validated or the object guard suffices.
Source: batch 7 task 1 review, reviewer note (2026-09-02).

items.title: install validates the stamp before writing kit-owned files
body: install rewrites every KIT_OWNED file before it reads the stamp, so a corrupt .houserules.json exits 2 with the target already updated. Pre-existing since batch 4; same order as the invalid-JSON path. Owner-candidate: decide whether the stamp read moves ahead of the writes.
Source: batch 7 task 1 review, reviewer note (2026-09-02).

items.title: The dependency-add eval query names its payload collision
body: The query names the project's tooling package, which collides with houserules.payload-runs-on-builtins when run in this repository, forcing a deviation disclosure every run; the judge cannot tell a designed trap from an accidental ambiguity.
Fix: name the repository's own devDependencies in the query, or add the collision to expected_behavior as an explicit judged criterion. Changing a scenario triggers process.evals-rerun.
Source: batch 7 branch review, template_defects 2 (2026-09-02).

items.title: implementer.md's Report section lists one field per line
body: After live_run and mode landed, the Report field list is one long single sentence; each contract change re-inflates it and makes template diffs hard to review. Restructure as one line per field, wording unchanged.
Changing implementer.md triggers process.evals-rerun; schedule with the next template batch.
Source: batch 7 branch review, template_defects 4 (2026-09-02).

items.title: One idPrefix predicate serves the flag and the stamp
body: install validates the --id-prefix flag with /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{0,7}$/ but the stamp guard (HR-027) accepts any non-empty string, so a hand-edited .houserules.json can carry a prefix init would refuse (' ', 'wi', 'TOOLONGPREFIX') and the next line writes it back. Two validators for one concept in one function.

RULED by the owner 2026-09-02: unify on the flag's regex (/^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{0,7}$/) as one shared predicate with one message, in the flag check and the stamp guard both. RED first; the HR-027 tests move to the shared message where applicable.
Source: batch 8 task 3 review, minor 4 (2026-09-02).

items.title: Pin the seeded eval scenario copies to their template sources
body: No gate pins .claude/evals/{dependency-add,docs-edit,seeded-violations}.json to their template/.claude/evals/ sources: dogfood parity covers KIT_OWNED only, and HR-025's batch 8 pin covers the deliverables schema pair. Batch 8 T5 made the dependency-add pair carry a judged criterion that must not drift; a one-sided edit would ship a seeded scenario that grades differently from the one this repository runs on itself.
Add a sync test beside the deliverables-schema pin for the three scenario copies. Exclude record.json: the root copy holds run sets and the template copy ships empty, so they differ by design.
Source: batch 8 task 5 review, minor 2 (2026-09-02).

items.title: implementer.md's tdd bullet carries the timing-key example inline
body: Ruling 18's first enforcement cost a Critical, a sanctioned amend, and a fix round: the batch 8 task 4 implementer re-ran the RED against checked-out pre-fix code after the fix existed and read the natural label as a statement about code state, not chronology.

Add the decisive example inline to the template's tdd bullet: a RED re-captured against pre-fix code after the fix exists is reconstructed; natural is chronology, not code state. Changing implementer.md triggers process.evals-rerun; schedule with the next template batch.
Source: batch 8 branch review, template_defects 2 (2026-09-02).

items.title: The dispatch protocol states that --ids IS the Knowledge list
body: Task-brief boilerplate carries a hand-filled --ids line nothing pins to the dispatch's Knowledge list; the batch 8 task 5 brief shipped the T3/T4 cli ids into a data-only task and only the implementer's cross-check caught it. The retrieval protocol implies the equality but never states it.

State it in the orchestrating skill's dispatch section and in the retrieval protocol text in template/tools/kb.mjs: the audit --ids value IS the dispatch's Knowledge list, generated from it, never typed separately. Add one skill sentence requiring a ledger line for every guard-caught controller slip (batch 8 branch review, template_defects 3). The kb.mjs retrieval-protocol change needs a scenario re-run per process.evals-rerun's body; schedule with HR-033.
Source: batch 8 branch review, template_defects 1 and 3 (2026-09-02).

items.title: The test suite cleans its mkdtemp scratch directories
body: tests/ has 21 mkdtempSync call sites across seven files and none removes its directory; every pnpm test run adds a full seeded project tree per init target. At the batch 9 task 2 review /tmp held 1714 orphaned houserules-target-* directories plus 89 kb-* and 15 ws-*, and a transient inode exhaustion had already broken one suite attempt (disclosed in the task 2 report).

Fix: give the mkdtemp sites cleanup — onTestFinished/afterEach with rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }), or one fixture helper that mints and registers scratch dirs. Behavior of the tests unchanged; the suite leaves /tmp as it found it.
Source: batch 9 task 2 review, controller escalation resolved (2026-09-03).

Rider (batch 9 branch review): land the knowledge entry houserules.tests-clean-scratch-dirs with the retrofit, so the rule has a loading path the moment the call sites are fixed. Summary: 'Every test that mints a scratch directory registers its removal at the mkdtemp site: onTestFinished/afterEach with rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }), or the shared fixture helper.' Area tests; the body names the 1714-orphan census and states the suite leaves /tmp as it found it.

items.title: The report status field ties to a non-empty concerns list
body: implementer.md defines DONE_WITH_CONCERNS only for the final chat message; nothing ties the report's status field to a non-empty concerns list. Batch 9 produced two reports whose file says DONE while the agent's answer and the ledger say DONE_WITH_CONCERNS (task 3; the dependency-add eval scenario). The report file is the artifact of record, so the divergence leaves the returned status ambiguous.

Fix: one sentence at the status bullet — set status to DONE_WITH_CONCERNS whenever concerns is non-empty; the answer message repeats the report's status verbatim. Changing implementer.md triggers process.evals-rerun.
Source: batch 9 branch review, template_defects 1 (2026-09-03).

items.title: The ledger bullet covers every controller slip, gate-caught or not
body: The orchestrating skill's ledger bullet binds only slips that a gate or && chain catches; a slip caught by inspection carries no logging duty. The gap showed the day the sentence shipped: the record-commit indent amend, caught by re-reading the diff stat and not by a gate, went unlogged, and a second formatting slip in the batch 9 finish repeated the class.

Fix: widen the bullet to every controller slip that forces a re-run, an amend, or a correction — gate-caught or not — logged when it happens. Skill-only change; no scenario covers the orchestrating skill, so no re-run is due.
Source: batch 9 branch review, template_defects 2 (2026-09-03).

items.title: Adopters can update their vendored kit when houserules releases changes
body: A project that adopted the kit has no defined path to newer kit versions. init and update stamp the running CLI's version into .houserules.json (bin/houserules.mjs writes { version, idPrefix }), but nothing reads the stamp back for comparison: an adopter learns of a new release nowhere, and no doc states the flow (bump the houserules dependency, run update, review the diff).

Shape: the CLI reports stamped-versus-running drift (update prints what version it upgrades from and to; files or a status command surfaces it read-only); README documents the adopter flow end to end. Details to the batch spec when scheduled.
Source: owner, 2026-09-03 (docs/design.md §5.19). Pairs with HR-039 — the release machinery makes a new version a real, announced event.

items.title: Semver releases via release-please with an alpha pre-release
body: RULED by the owner 2026-09-03 (docs/design.md §5.19): versioning is semver; changelogs are generated from the conventional commits; the tool is release-please; the first release is a pre-release under the alpha dist-tag; the GitHub upstream is created right after the alpha-state tasks are done. Until the upstream exists, decision 3's constraint stands: no remote, no gh repo create, no npm publish.

Shape: local groundwork can land before the upstream (release-please config and manifest, prerelease alpha versioning strategy, the release-type choice for a single-package pnpm repo, CHANGELOG bootstrap); the automation itself runs on GitHub and activates when the upstream is created. Publishing to npm under the alpha dist-tag follows as the first release.

RULED by the owner 2026-09-03 (batch 11 gate): alpha state = HR-040 + HR-038 + this item's local groundwork, gated as batch 11; completing that batch constitutes alpha state, and the upstream creation follows immediately.
Source: owner, 2026-09-03; release-please chosen over git-cliff and changesets at the ruling.

items.title: One evals rerun pays the live_run capture form and the collision-line reword
body: Batch 10 produced three evidence-capture findings of one class (stderr redirected after the target, a command with no per-command capture, a `; cat` tail owning the recorded exit) and one undecidable eval line: dependency-add expected_behavior[1] presumes a separate dependency-free payload manifest, so a single-manifest repository passes it only by judgment — the fifth record notes the call verbatim.

Fix, one batch, one evals rerun for both: (a) the implementer.md live_run bullet states the canonical capture form — one command per entry, captured as `<command> > <file> 2>&1`, the recorded exit is that command's own, no `;` or `|` tails; (b) dependency-add expected_behavior[1] in both scenario copies rewords to two decidable outcomes — with a payload manifest present, place the dependency outside it and disclose the collision in concerns; with the root manifest as the only manifest, keep the payload import-free and state the placement reasoning in the report.
Source: batch 10 branch review, template_defects 1 and 2 (2026-09-03).

items.title: validate rejects a terminal-status report with a null self_audit
body: A task report with status DONE or DONE_WITH_CONCERNS and self_audit null passes tools/kb.sh validate. Batch 11 task 3's implementer was interrupted mid-finalization by a session restart; the on-disk report looked schema-complete and only the controller's null probe caught the gap.

Fix: validate fails when a task-report's status is terminal and self_audit is null. The retrieval protocol's write-then-fill flow keeps working: the pre-fill report carries no terminal claim the validator trusts. Template tools/kb.mjs + root sync; deliverables schema unchanged unless the check fits there better.

Extension (batch 12 branch review, template_defects 2): the same validate change also rejects a task-report whose self_audit.summary.skipped is greater than 0, naming the --report flag in the message — a fix-round audit recorded without --report validated cleanly and cost a follow-up round.
Source: batch 11 branch review, template_defects 1 (2026-09-03); batch 12 branch review, template_defects 2 (2026-09-03).

items.title: Reviewer prescriptions state the invariant plus the observed instance

items.title: The release version bump breaks CI: stale dogfood stamp and a pre-release-blind test regex
body: The 0.2.0-alpha release commit turned main red: tests/dogfood.test.mjs expects the repo stamp to equal the running VERSION, but .houserules.json still says 0.1.0 (nobody ran update after the bump); tests/init.test.mjs asserts the stamped version matches /^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/, which rejects every pre-release version although the owner ruled pre-release alpha versions the norm (design.md 5.19).

Consider: every future release PR merge needs the restamp — either document it in the release runbook or make CI tolerant of the one-commit lag; decide in the spec.

items.title: Rewrite the toolchain as one static binary (Tier 2)
body: RULED by the owner 2026-09-03: go straight to Tier 2 — no Tier 0 (version-manager-provided Node) and no Tier 1 (bundled-JS binaries) interim steps. The kit becomes runs-anywhere: one compiled, statically linked houserules binary replaces the Node toolchain end to end.

Scope: rewrite bin/houserules.mjs, template/tools/kb.mjs, and template/tools/backlog.mjs in RUST (RULED 2026-09-04, design.md 5.21); the vendored tools/kb.sh and tools/backlog.sh become thin POSIX shims that exec the houserules binary on PATH; every existing behavior carries over under the current suite's contracts (init/update, KIT_OWNED sync and the stamp with its drift line, render, check, audit, validate, the backlog commands). The payload invariant houserules.payload-runs-on-builtins redefines to one static binary plus POSIX shell — a docs/design.md amendment and an owner ruling at spec time.

Migration: the JS suite pins today's behavior; port tests alongside the rewrite; parity gates (byte-identical render output, identical audit JSON on the same range) hold before the JS path retires. Multi-batch work; the spec decides the slicing.
Source: owner, 2026-09-03 (Tier 2 direct, superseding the tiered distribution proposal).

COMPLETE 2026-09-08, batch 20 (Tier 2 closes): phase 3 put the payload in the binary and self-flipped the repository (batch 18, main c82fe1e); phase 4 wired the release channels (batch 19, main 253746a); phase 5 retired everything JS -- bin/houserules.mjs, the frozen corpus and make-corpus, the vitest layer, package.json/pnpm/node, and the shipped-but-inert payload engines -- with the parity contract re-baselined as Rust-generated goldens and a permanent residue gate in mise run lint. items.title: release-please's release-type still needs the package.json HR-047 retired
body: PRE-MERGE: this fires on the next push to main, not at a later release attempt. Batch 20 T3 (HR-047, docs/specs/2026-09-07-batch-20-phase5.md §2) retires package.json along with the rest of the JS toolchain. release-please-config.json's packages['.'].release-type is still "node", with no package-name override, and .github/workflows/release-please.yml runs release-please-action@v5.0.0 on every push to main -- not only when cutting a release.

Derived from the pinned v17.11.2 source (release-please-action@v5.0.0 resolves release-please ^17.6.0), not a config-string reading, per process.wiring-checks-run-the-resolution: BaseStrategy.buildReleasePullRequest calls getBranchComponent() to name the release branch. Unlike its sibling getComponent(), getBranchComponent() is NOT guarded by includeComponentInTag -- it always calls getDefaultComponent(), which falls through to `this.packageName ?? getDefaultPackageName()` since no package-name is configured. The Node strategy's getDefaultPackageName() reads package.json through getPkgJsonContents(); a missing file makes getPkgJsonContents() catch FileNotFoundError and throw MissingRequiredFileError naming package.json, 'node', and this repository.

HR-068 (the tag-push token gap) does NOT shield this: HR-068 is about release.yml never starting after a tag pushes, which happens strictly later in the pipeline than this failure. Once T3's branch merges, release-please-action throws on that very push, before any PR opens -- not gated behind HR-068/HR-069's step-two release track, and not something a later release attempt discovers first.

Re-scoped as a pre-merge owner decision (fix round 1, task-3-review.json important finding 4 -- the original wording hedged the impact as 'may fail ... or error outright' and scheduled it behind HR-068/HR-069, which the derived call path above shows is wrong on both counts). The choice among a different release-type (rust: needs the workspace root to carry a [package]; simple: needs a version.txt this repository does not have) or node with an explicit package-name pointing at a file that still exists is a config ruling this checkout cannot close: it needs a real release-please run against the chosen config, not a source reading alone.
Source: batch 20 T3 (HR-047) implementation, discovered while removing package.json per spec §2; re-derived and re-scoped in fix round 1 (task-3-review.json, important finding 4).

RULED 2026-09-08 (design.md 5.43): release-type rust at crates/houserules, landed on the batch-20 branch pre-merge; plain v-tags kept; extra-files re-derived; local validation as far as possible, live proof at the owner-attended first release.

APPLIED 2026-09-08 (batch 20 T5). release-please-config.json's packages["crates/houserules"] now names release-type "rust" (packages['.'] and "node" gone); .release-please-manifest.json's key moved with it. extra-files: the redundant crates/houserules/Cargo.toml toml/jsonpath entry is gone (the Rust strategy already emits that update natively, source-verified); README.md and template/.github/workflows/knowledge.yml now read /README.md and /template/.github/workflows/knowledge.yml (a leading / anchors an extra-file to the repository root once the package sits off root -- BaseStrategy.addPath, v17.11.2 source, docs/runbook.md's HR-073 section carries the file:line citations). changelog-path: "/CHANGELOG.md" keeps the existing root changelog rather than letting the strategy start a second one under crates/houserules/. Cargo.lock gets no extra-files entry: its own recorded version for the local package self-heals on the next cargo build/check/test (verified live by a temporary version bump and revert, t5-evidence/cargo-check-version-bump-self-heal.log). A verified, permanent side effect of the path move, not a bug: release-please now attributes a commit to this package only when it touches crates/houserules/** (CommitSplit, v17.11.2 source) -- a docs- or knowledge-only commit no longer opens a release PR, correct for a repository whose one shipped artifact is that crate's binary. Local validation: a new cargo test (crates/houserules/tests/release_please_config.rs) pins the manifest/config package-path match, the rust release-type, the extra-files leading-/ anchor, and the absence of any package.json mention; a schema-conformance script checks the config against the pinned v17.11.2 JSON schema (t5-evidence/config-schema-conformance-check.py); `dist plan --tag=v0.2.0-alpha` stays exit 0. Unproven until the first live release (HR-068 step two): whether release-please's own buildReleasePullRequest actually opens a mergeable PR under this exact config against a real repository -- no local run can substitute for that, disclosed in docs/runbook.md's own HR-073 section.

items.title: CI's mise-action pin (v2026.9.2) has no documented update habit yet
body: PR #8's CI failed on every job (checks, rust x3, check-commit) when jdx/mise-action@v4 resolved an unpinned `version` input to 'latest' and that latest was v2026.9.3, a version GitHub never finished publishing a release for. Every job's log shows the identical failure: `curl -fsSL https://github.com/jdx/mise/releases/download/v2026.9.3/mise-v2026.9.3-<target>.<ext> --output ...` returning `curl: (22)`/`(56) The requested URL returned error: 404`, retried 6 times each (batch 20 T6, t6-evidence/pr8-ci-checks-job-log.txt, pr8-ci-rust-ubuntu-job-log.txt, pr8-ci-rust-macos-job-log.txt, pr8-ci-rust-windows-job-log.txt, pr8-ci-check-commit-job-log.txt). The GitHub API confirms the gap directly: `GET /repos/jdx/mise/releases/tags/v2026.9.3` 404s (t6-evidence/mise-v2026.9.3-release.json) while `GET /repos/jdx/mise/releases/latest` returns tag_name v2026.9.2 with all 46 assets (t6-evidence/mise-latest-release.json, mise-v2026.9.2-release.json).

The fix (this item's own origin) pins `version: 2026.9.2` on every jdx/mise-action step in .github/workflows/ci.yml, verified against the action's own current action.yml and README for the input name and bare-version value format (t6-evidence/mise-action-v4-action.yml, mise-action-v4-README.md), and against the v2026.9.2 release asset URLs the action's own source constructs (t6-evidence/mise-action-v4-src-index.ts), probed live and returning HTTP 302 for every target this repository's CI matrix runs (t6-evidence/probe-v2026.9.2-asset-urls.log).

A hand-pinned version is now a deliberate dependency with no update habit: nothing in this repository re-checks it, so it drifts behind upstream's real releases the same way houserules.rust-toolchain-bumps-use-stable's own procedure exists to keep the rust pin current on purpose rather than by accident. Candidate remedies (this item carries the question, not the answer): (a) a docs/runbook.md maintenance-notes entry naming a periodic check -- `GET /repos/jdx/mise/releases/latest` compared against the pinned value -- before bumping it; (b) a periodic bump ritual (a scheduled reminder or a recurring backlog item) that re-verifies the target release has its full asset set live, the same check this item's own fix performed by hand, before moving the pin. Owner picks.
Source: batch 20 T6, the merge-unblocking incident fix.

Live proof (batch 20 T6 fix round 1): the pin holds across every ci.yml OS through four successive pushes while HR-084's own windows-latest layers got peeled back -- mise 2026.9.2 installs (fresh download, verified checksums) on checks/rust-ubuntu/rust-macos/check-commit every run, and on rust-windows too (`mise --version` reports "2026.9.2 windows-x64 (2026-09-07)", run 34218918139, job 102037165620); windows-latest's own remaining failures are downstream of mise entirely (HR-084, HR-085), never mise-action itself.

items.title: Windows CI's first real run finds tests/fixtures/** CRLF-corrupted, breaking two check_parity byte compares
body: HR-083's mise pin unblocked mise-action's setup step on every ci.yml job, so windows-latest's `rust` job ran `cargo test` for real for the first time in this batch (every earlier CI attempt on this branch, and on 6d92aee before it, failed at mise-action before cargo test ever started there) -- this is a first real signal, not a regression HR-083 introduced. Two check_parity.rs tests failed there: `check_knowledge_matches_the_frozen_mini_corpus` (stdout diverged: actual "" against the frozen `knowledge: ok\n`) and `check_knowledge_matches_the_frozen_mini_stale_corpus` (stderr diverged: the actual run additionally flags `.claude/rules/standing-rules.md` as stale, absent from the frozen golden, and reports `CLAUDE.md: 14279 bytes` against the frozen `14257 bytes`) (batch 20 T6, t6-evidence/pr8-post-fix-rust-windows-FAIL-job-log.txt, run 34215459708 job 102026042204).

Root cause, confirmed for the mini-stale byte divergence: `tests/fixtures/mini-stale/CLAUDE.md` is 14257 bytes on a Linux checkout (`wc -c`, matching the frozen golden exactly) and `git check-attr text` reports it "unspecified". `.gitattributes` already marks `tests/corpus/**` and `tests/goldens/**` `-text` for exactly this failure class -- its own comment cites the identical break on PR #6, run 34056471594 -- but nothing protects `tests/fixtures/**` the same way, so the windows-latest runner's default `core.autocrlf` converts every fixture file's checked-out LF to CRLF, growing CLAUDE.md by 22 bytes and flipping standing-rules.md from current to stale because its checked-out bytes no longer match a freshly rendered copy bit for bit.

The `mini_corpus` failure (empty stdout in place of `knowledge: ok\n`) is not root-caused to the same certainty and is recorded as observed, not diagnosed further, per knowledge-base.state-only-the-source.

Candidate fix (ready, mirrors the two existing `.gitattributes` entries): add `tests/fixtures/mini/** -text`, `tests/fixtures/mini-bad/** -text`, and `tests/fixtures/mini-stale/** -text`; the same reasoning also reaches `tests/fixtures/batch14-workspace/** -text`, today equally unprotected despite houserules.corpus-batch14-fixtures-are-committed's own "verbatim" intent. Re-run the windows-latest leg live before closing this item.

Blocks a fully green windows-latest leg on batch-20's PR #8. Filed separately rather than folded into HR-083: batch 20 T6's own scope was the mise pin alone, one commit, and this is an unrelated root cause (git line-ending checkout behavior, not action version resolution).
Source: batch 20 T6, the live CI run after the mise-pin fix (t6-evidence/pr8-post-fix-rust-windows-FAIL-job-log.txt).

FIX ROUND 1 (batch 20 T6, controller re-scope: implements in this batch, process.every-main-commit-is-ci-green). True root cause, traced through git history rather than left as the candidate guess above: these seven fixture directories lived under tests/corpus/fixtures/ and so carried tests/corpus/** -text (batch 16 T1, commit a0cebcd) until batch 20 T3's relocation (commit e36c4b2, "chore(tests): relocate tests/corpus/fixtures to tests/fixtures") moved them to tests/fixtures/ without a matching .gitattributes update -- a rename path rules do not follow, not a gap that predated Windows consumers. Landed as tests/fixtures/** -text (commit 18111f0), covering all seven relocated directories at once (git add --renormalize changed zero files -- every blob was already pure LF). Both named failures are fixed and reverified live: check_parity.rs carries no failure in any windows-latest run since.

The mini_corpus mechanism is now confirmed, not merely observed: check.rs's check_base does an exact string compare between each on-disk generated file (.claude/rules/*.md, the knowledge skill) and a freshly rendered LF copy, and check_budget counts raw bytes/lines -- CRLF-inflating mini's own generated files creates a spurious stale finding, and check-knowledge prints empty stdout for ANY finding (confirmed against tests/goldens/check/mini-bad.json, whose golden stdout is also ""), exactly matching the observed empty-stdout symptom. Same cause as the byte-count divergence, one fix (tests/fixtures/** -text) covers both, as predicted.

Two further, previously-hidden windows-latest layers surfaced and were fixed in the same fix round, each only reachable once the layer before it stopped aborting cargo test early (plain `cargo test` stops at the first failing binary): (1) commit_msg_hook.rs's hook_path() built its path through Path::canonicalize, which the pinned rustc 1.98.1's own docs confirm produces a Windows-only `\\?\`-prefixed extended-length path incompatible with an external command-line consumer -- Git-for-Windows' sh could not open it, exit 127 on all 7 tests, run 34217792336 job 102033559639; fixed (commit 816e45e) by building the path directly from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR without canonicalizing. (2) dogfood.rs's generated_files_are_fresh_relative_to_knowledge ran render --check against this repository's own live .claude/rules/**/SKILL.md -- never given -text protection at all, since the consumer is new rather than the leg: windows-latest has run cargo test in this repository's own ci.yml since 0bb27a0 (2026-09-04, before batch 20), but dogfood.rs and its no-JS-predecessor render --check case arrived only with batch 20 T1's test port (2174a9f), so no Windows run had reached this comparison; all eight files reported stale, run 34218413737 job 102035560326; fixed (commit c9014d5) by extending -text to .claude/rules/** and .claude/skills/project-knowledge/**, covering render_all()'s entire output set exactly.

A fourth, structurally different failure remains after all three fixes (install.rs's init_reports_a_render_failure_on_broken_project_data_as_one_usage_error, run 34218918139 job 102037165620): filed separately as HR-085, since its mechanism is not CRLF/git-checkout at all (the seeded broken JSON is written at runtime via fs::write, never through git) and was not confidently root-caused despite substantial tracing. windows-latest is not green yet; the batch's merge remains blocked on HR-085.

HISTORY CORRECTED (batch 20 T6 fix round 3, task-6-review issue 1). The FIX ROUND 1 paragraph above used to say windows-latest never existed in this repository's own ci.yml before batch 20 T3/T4's Rust port added the OS matrix. That was false: 0bb27a0 (2026-09-04, batch 16's phase-1 port, on main before batch 20) added the rust job with os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest] running cargo test. The paragraph now states the true shield -- the consumer is new, not the leg -- and .gitattributes's own comment block carries the same correction. Only the reason changed; every measured failure, run id and fix in this item stands.

CLOSED (batch 20 T6 fix round 2). The sentence above -- "windows-latest is not green yet; the batch's merge remains blocked on HR-085" -- is superseded: HR-085's mechanism was confirmed (a single join keeping an embedded slash on Windows) and fixed at commit 575651e. Run 34221494012 shows every ci.yml job green, windows-latest included (job 102045415106, 20 test binaries ok, 0 failed). This item's own three fixes are unchanged and green in that same run, which is the first windows-latest run to reach every test binary. Ticked done at batch 20.

items.title: windows-latest install.rs path pin built its expected path with one join, keeping an embedded slash
body: Discovered live while landing HR-084's fix round 1 (batch 20 T6): once the three CRLF/checkout-format layers HR-084 tracks were fixed, windows-latest's `rust` job reached crates/houserules/tests/install.rs for the first time and failed init_reports_a_render_failure_on_broken_project_data_as_one_usage_error (run 34218918139, job 102037165620, t6-fix1-evidence/windows-postfix4-job-log.txt). The test seeds a deliberately broken knowledge/process.json ("{"), runs `houserules init --dir <tempdir>`, and asserts stderr starts with `<tempdir>/knowledge/process.json: invalid JSON (`; the panic (install.rs:481) shows the actual stderr as `C:\Users\RUNNER~1\AppData\Local\Temp\.tmpCUW8io\knowledge\process.json: invalid JSON (EOF while parsing an object at line 1 column 1)\n` -- textually indistinguishable from the expected prefix pattern at a glance, yet `starts_with` fails.

Not CRLF: the seeded content is written at runtime via std::fs::write, which never passes through git's checkout filters (.gitattributes governs git checkin/checkout only), so this is a structurally different mechanism from HR-084's three fixes, all of which involved a git-checked-out generated or fixture file compared against fresh in-memory content.

Ruled out by tracing the full call chain (fix round 1, batch 20 T6): (a) resolve_like_node's own \\?\-prefix stripping (node_path.rs) -- the input `--dir` argument is already absolute and carries no prefix, so strip_verbatim_disk_prefix and normalize_lexically are no-ops here, confirmed by reading every Component the path yields; (b) canonicalize anywhere in the production call chain (seed -> render_and_report -> load_base -> read_json_value) -- grep across crates/houserules/src finds no canonicalize call outside dev-only bin/ gates, none of which init's path touches; (c) extra or reordered stderr content -- the full captured stderr (shown verbatim in the panic's `{stderr:?}`) contains nothing before the path, ruling out a preceding warning line; (d) file-read-order or content corruption -- the reported path and the exact serde_json EOF-at-1:1 message are consistent with the test's own seeded `"{"` byte being read intact; (e) an adjacent, structurally identical test (init_reports_an_unparsable_pre_existing_marker_as_a_named_error_exit_2, a direct target-root file, not one found via directory listing) passes in the same run, narrowing the difference to something specific about reading a file via knowledge/'s own fs::read_dir listing versus a fixed marker path, but no further mechanism was confirmed.

Candidate remedies (open, owner/next investigator picks): (a) reproduce on an actual Windows machine or a hosted Windows shell with RUST_BACKTRACE=1 and a temporary eprintln! of both the expected and actual strings side by side -- the report-writing agent had no Windows execution access, only the CI log's own captured panic text; (b) suspect tempfile::tempdir()'s own Windows path form (short 8.3 segments are visible in the runner's TEMP, e.g. RUNNER~1) interacting with some as-yet-unidentified normalization difference between the test's own `dir.path().join(...)` and the path load_base ultimately builds; (c) instrument install.rs's own test to print both sides via assert_eq! instead of assert! before the next windows-latest attempt, so the actual divergence is visible in the CI log directly rather than inferred.
Blocks windows-latest going green; HR-084's own three fixes are otherwise confirmed complete and live-verified. Source: batch 20 T6 fix round 1 (t6-fix1-evidence/windows-postfix4-job-log.txt).

FIX ROUND 2 (batch 20 T6, escalated one model tier). Mechanism confirmed from artifacts, not guessed: the test built its expected path with ONE join, `dir.path().join("knowledge/process.json")`. rustc 1.98.1's library/std/src/path.rs (PathBuf::_push) appends a relative path verbatim after one MAIN_SEPARATOR_STR, and re-joins components with that separator only behind a verbatim (\\?\) prefix, which a tempfile path never carries. So the expectation kept its embedded / (`...\knowledge/process.json`) while the binary printed rules::model::load_base's own `root.join("knowledge")` then `dir.join(name)` (`...\knowledge\process.json`). One character. Of the three candidate remedies above, (b) was closest: the tempdir path form was innocent, the join shape was not; (c) was unnecessary once the two sides were placed side by side.

Three artifacts carry the derivation, no Windows execution needed: (1) the panic in run 34220012072, job 102040656623 shows the actual string ending `\knowledge\process.json`; (2) load_base (crates/houserules/src/rules/model.rs, the topic-file loop) builds that name with two joins; (3) that same red run passes install.rs's two structural controls, each of which compares a printed path against the binary's own stderr. The marker pin is init_reports_an_unparsable_pre_existing_marker_as_a_named_error_exit_2, a one-component dir.path().join(".houserules.json"). The settings pin is init_reports_a_scalar_hooks_value_as_a_named_error_exit_2 and init_reports_a_scalar_session_start_value_as_a_named_error_exit_2, which assert_eq! stderr against format!("{}: ...", settings_path.display()), where the test's dir.path().join(".claude/settings.json") and the binary's target.join(SETTINGS_PATH) build the path from the identical string. The marker pin proves the tempdir prefix round-trips through the binary exactly; the settings pin proves an identical-string join interoperates. Together they leave the separator as the only difference.

CLAUSE NAMED TEST-BY-TEST (batch 20 T6 fix round 3, task-6-review issue 4). The review read the settings clause as citing a settings-path string assertion that install.rs does not carry. Re-derived against the file at dea7da1: it does carry two, at the settings_path sites in init_reports_a_scalar_hooks_value_as_a_named_error_exit_2 and init_reports_a_scalar_session_start_value_as_a_named_error_exit_2, and both are ok in the red job's own log (t6-fix2-evidence/windows-red-job-102040656623.txt). The clause is not weakened, since that would ship a false statement; it now names each control by test function so a reader finds the assertion instead of hunting for it.

Fixed at commit 575651e: the expected path is now built component by component, the way load_base builds it, and the assertion prints both sides so the next divergence is readable from one CI log. The assertion is not loosened. Live proof: run 34221494012, job 102045415106, `rust (windows-latest)` green -- install.rs 24 passed, 0 failed, and every one of the 20 test binaries ok, including the six no windows-latest run in this batch had reached before (read_parity, release_please_config, render_parity, update, validate_stats_audit_parity, version -- plain `cargo test` stops at the first failing binary, and `install` sorts ahead of all six). checks, check-commit, rust (ubuntu-latest) and rust (macos-latest) are green in the same run. Every ci run before it on this branch failed: t6-fix2-evidence/ci-runs-on-batch-20.txt enumerates them. Evidence: t6-fix2-evidence/windows-green-job-102045415106.txt, green-job-list-34221494012.txt. The gotcha is filed as houserules.path-pins-mirror-the-code (commit 9ef8d65).

items.title: validate and check-report-claims both accept a textList shredded into one string per character
body: Found at batch 20 T6 fix round 2 and filed by its review (task-6-review.json issue 2, minor). A `+=` of a string onto a `textList` field appends one list item per character. `houserules validate` accepts the result, because `$defs/text` requires only minLength 1 and every character is a valid string, and `houserules check-report-claims` accepts it too, because it reads command/output pairs, not prose shape. Only a human reading the field caught it.

Re-derived in fix round 3, not restated: .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-07-batch-20/t6-fix3-evidence/degenerate-self-review-probe.json is the T6 report with self_review replaced by list("degenerate textList probe"), 25 single-character items. `houserules validate` on it exits 0 with errors [] (probe-validate.log) and `houserules check-report-claims` on it exits 0 with "no claim mismatches found" (probe-check-report-claims.log). The review's own probe reported the same on a 21-item list.

Blast radius: nine textList fields across the four deliverable kinds -- taskReport.self_review, taskReport.concerns, taskReview.strengths, reReview.out_of_scope, reReview.verdict.open, branchReview.strengths, branchReview.recommendations, and the two retrospective `tasks` lists. The enumeration is executable and rerunnable: `python3 .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-07-batch-20/t6-fix3-evidence/enumerate-textlist-fields.py` walks $defs for `#/$defs/textList` refs and prints each field with its count. Its run reports 9 for .claude/schemas/deliverables.json and 9 for template/.claude/schemas/deliverables.json, the copy this repository ships, so the gap reaches every adopter.

Design choice for the owner, not settled here. (a) A minLength on textList items in deliverables.json: cheap, declarative, and it ships with the schema, but any single threshold is arbitrary and a legitimate short item (a two-word recommendation) could trip it. (b) A check-report-claims rule flagging an array dominated by single-character strings: it keeps the schema honest about shape versus quality, can state the ratio it measured, and can carry an exception, but it lives only where the checker runs and needs its own regression test. Pick one before implementing.

Not fixed inside T6: the schema is outside that task's scope and quality.no-compat-softening forbids a partial patch that would look like a guard. The round-2 incident itself is disclosed in the T6 report's self_review and concerns.

items.title: a fresh init's own docs area glob is dead until docs/ gets real content
body: Found live-running HR-074 (batch 21 T1): template/knowledge/areas.json's docs area declares docs/** among its globs, and a brand-new `houserules init` never creates anything under docs/ -- CLAUDE.md, knowledge/**, backlog/**, and .claude/** all match immediately, but docs/** alone starts dead. check-knowledge --dir <freshly-init'd repo> fails on the very first run with `knowledge/areas.json.docs.paths: "docs/**" matches no tracked file`, contradicting the "next: houserules check-knowledge && houserules check-backlog" line init itself prints.

Reproduced live: git init a scratch dir, `houserules init --dir .`, `houserules check-knowledge --dir .` -- exit 1, the one line above, no docs/ content anywhere yet. tools/** does not share the defect (`.github/workflows/knowledge.yml` already matches .github/**, tools' other glob).

Out of scope for HR-074 itself: fixing this means editing template/knowledge/areas.json, a template file HR-074's own task brief named out of bounds ("NO template/agent/eval file changes beyond the schema copy -- if a fix would touch one, FLAG"). Candidate fixes for whoever picks this up: drop the bare docs/** glob (fold docs into the same treatment as tools, or into global/process's own empty-list precedent), or seed a placeholder file under docs/ alongside the other SEED_ONCE files.

Ruled in-branch by the task-1 review (fix round 1, important issue 3): a scope guard on the implementer is not a licence for the defect to ship, and the fix is small and bounded. Fixed: template/docs/README.md ships via SEED_ONCE (install.rs), giving the docs area's docs/** glob a real file every init writes; verified restoring knowledge: ok on a fresh init and keeping `houserules for docs/design.md` at ["docs", "global"].

items.title: houserules update never backfills docs/README.md on a pre-batch-21 install
body: Filed by the task-1 fix round 2 review (task-1-review-r2.json, new_breakage 3). docs/README.md (HR-087) closes the fresh-init path but not the update path: SEED_ONCE seeds a file once and never touches it again (install.rs's own documented contract), so an install that predates this batch and has no docs/ content stays broken after update.

Reproduced by the reviewer at HEAD: take an install that predates this change with no docs/ content, run `houserules update --dir .` (which still prints the same `next: houserules check-knowledge && houserules check-backlog` line), and check-knowledge exits 1 with `knowledge/areas.json.docs.paths: "docs/**" matches no tracked file (git ls-files)`; no docs/README.md appears.

Same class as HR-087, reached by the other command: the kit's own seeded areas.json declares a glob its own seed leaves unmatched, for an adopter who did nothing wrong. Exposure today is nil (the kit is an unpublished 0.2.0-alpha, the tag-pilot adoption is parked at PP-1-02, and this repository has real docs/ content), and the failure is loud, named, and self-explanatory -- why this is filed rather than fixed in-branch, unlike HR-087.

Do not fix by making update backfill SEED_ONCE: that contradicts install.rs's own documented "seeds once and never touches again" contract and opens a design question this item does not settle -- backfill semantics generally, versus an adopter who deleted a seed file on purpose, versus a documented manual step printed by update itself. Pick one before implementing.

items.title: Harden the public repository: rulesets, Dependabot, CodeQL, SHA-pinned actions, cargo deny, attestations
body: Owner request 2026-09-11 after a settings review against the OpenSSF SCM best practices and the Scorecard checks. Finding that drove it: the main ruleset targeted no branch at all (its ref_name include list was empty; /rules/branches/main returned []), so main was unprotected despite the ruleset existing.

Repository settings (applied through the REST API, no file): main ruleset now targets ~DEFAULT_BRANCH, requires the five ci jobs as status checks (strict), dismisses stale reviews, and requires thread resolution; a tags ruleset blocks deletion, update, and non-fast-forward on every tag; merge commits and squash merges are off, head branches auto-delete, update-branch is on; wiki and projects are off, Discussions is on; Dependabot alerts and security updates are on; CodeQL runs as an advanced setup (.github/workflows/codeql.yml, rust and actions) because the default-setup REST API rejects `rust` although the UI supports it, so default setup is off; the Actions policy is selected actions (GitHub-owned, verified, plus jdx/mise-action, googleapis/release-please-action, swatinem/rust-cache) with full-SHA pinning required, a read-only default token, and no PR approval by workflows.

Tracked-tree changes: .github/dependabot.yml (cargo and github-actions, chore prefix with scope); .github/CODEOWNERS; every uses: in ci.yml and release-please.yml pinned to a full commit SHA with the version as a comment, top-level permissions read-only with write scopes at job level; dist-workspace.toml gains github-attestations and the github-action-commits table so the regenerated release.yml is pinned and attests every artifact; deny.toml plus cargo deny check in mise run lint; cargo test --locked and clippy --locked; rust-version in crates/houserules/Cargo.toml declares the major.minor of the mise pin as the floor (an exact patch broke the macOS dist legs, whose runner ships the .0 patch).

Not done, by ruling: required signed commits (the owner does not sign today). Not available: secret scanning non-provider patterns and validity checks stay disabled on a user-owned public repository (the REST PATCH returns 200 and leaves them off; both belong to the paid Secret Protection tier).

Batch attribution (owner ruling, 2026-09-11, batch 21 report): this item landed as an owner-driven side PR during batch 21's window, not as batch-21 task work; batch=21 records the window so the done state carries a batch (the check-backlog warns retire).

items.title: Dependabot PRs fail check-commit and dist plan; auto-merge minor and patch updates
body: Owner request 2026-09-11 on the first Dependabot PRs (#10 merged by hand, #11 open). Two structural failures and one policy: (1) Dependabot's generated body carries a compare link over 100 characters, so process.conventional-commits fails in both check-commit and the audit; (2) a bump inside the generated release.yml fails dist's `plan` job, which checks the file against its own generation; (3) the owner wants minor and patch updates merged without a human, and major updates reviewed by the code owner.

Fixes: `commits_in` now reads the author name (%an) and `CommitsCheck::violation` exempts a `[bot]`-authored commit from body_line_max alone (subject and body_absent still apply; tests in audit.rs and check_commit.rs). The ruling is recorded in process.conventional-commits (root and template). dist-workspace.toml sets allow-dirty = ["ci"] so Dependabot may maintain the pins inside release.yml; the github-action-commits table stays the regeneration seed. .github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml enables GitHub auto-merge (rebase, the ruleset's only method) for semver-minor and semver-patch through dependabot/fetch-metadata; repository allow_auto_merge is on and the action is on the Actions allow-list.

Known limit, deliberate: auto-merge acts with GITHUB_TOKEN, so the resulting push to main starts no workflow (houserules.default-token-tags-start-no-workflows); release-please catches up on the next human push. HR-068's token decision can lift this later. PR #11 (a major, actions/checkout in release.yml) stays for the owner's review; a `@dependabot rebase` after this lands re-runs its checks.

Batch attribution (owner ruling, 2026-09-11, batch 21 report): this item landed as an owner-driven side PR during batch 21's window, not as batch-21 task work; batch=21 records the window so the done state carries a batch (the check-backlog warns retire).

items.title: Retire diff-shape-gate as a completed, expired proof
body: RULED by the controller (batch 21, derived and verified end to end at task-3-review.json issue 3): crates/houserules/src/bin/diff-shape-gate.rs is an EXPIRED ONE-SHOT PROOF, retired rather than repaired. items.title: Archive sweep: retired backlog items and knowledge entries leave the active set
body: Owner request (2026-09-11): after every batch, sweep the whole knowledge base and the backlog. Done backlog items; superseded, deprecated, or stale knowledge entries; and every other item whose status marks it as no longer relevant for future development move to an archive. The goal is an active knowledge base and backlog free of old data.

The archive stays readable: a history analysis can still reach every archived item. Archiving moves data; it never deletes it. knowledge-base.ids-are-permanent constrains the design: an archived entry id stays resolvable.

Design to settle at spec time: where the archive lives (for example backlog/archive/ and knowledge/archive/), how check-knowledge, check-backlog, and render treat archived files, whether the sweep is a houserules subcommand, and where the batch lifecycle runs it (a close-out step in the orchestrating or finishing skill).

items.title: Prune every code comment to current-state description; raise the in-code docs rule
body: Owner request (2026-09-11): sweep all comments in all code files and prune them. No comment documents history. A comment describes what is current: concisely, precisely, and without unnecessary detail.
One or more subagents run the sweep (dispatched sequentially, per process.sequential-agents), template/ copies included.

On this occasion, iterate a standing rule that maintains a high in-code documentation standard: extend or supersede writing-style.code-comments and writing-style.doc-comments so the standard names the pruning of history narration; the template knowledge copies ship the same rule.

items.title: Downstream template updates with adopter-modified markers
body: Owner request (2026-09-11): the kit controls the files in template/ and must be able to update them and their contents downstream to adopters through houserules update.
Conversely, an adopter must be able to mark items they adopted but then changed to fit their needs, so houserules update does not overwrite them.

Design to settle at spec time: the ownership model per file class (KIT_OWNED, SEED_ONCE, PREFIXED today), the marker an adopter sets and where it lives, conflict reporting when the kit updates content the adopter modified, and the granularity (whole file versus entry or item). The same design should settle HR-089's open backfill question.
